To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

oral administration of the environmental carcinogen benzo[a] pyrene (BP) to CD2F1 mice at a high dose of 125 mg/kg for 5 days in the presence of dextran sulfate (DSS) induced colon tumors both at Weeks 3 and 4.
the combination of BP with DSS-induced inflammation is a novel, rapid, and useful colon carcinogenic model.
oral administration of benzo[a] pyrene (BP), a potent environmental mutagen/cancer, to mice induces adenocarcinomata in the colon in the presence of DSS-induced inflammation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism(s) of colon tumorigenesis in the BP/DSS model.
the elucidation of mechanisms by which the environmental mutagen/cancerogen BP causes mutations and carcinomas in the mouse colonic mucosa.

the mechanisms of the development of colon tumors, and our BP/DSS model will provide a useful system for studying the mechanisms by which mutagenic events in normal cells can lead to the development of tumors in the mouse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inflammation in a tissue which is primed with mutagens, in the presence of carcinogens or mutagens, can lead to tumor development.
, in this model, BP induced mutations lead to adenocarinomas in the colon in the presence of DSS-induced inflammation, a tissue which does not normally respond to BP.
, in the BP/DSS model, the mutagenic events induced by BP in a tissue (the colon) which is not a target organ of BP are associated with subsequent adenocarcinogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BP/DSS-induced colonic inflammation is a key to tumor development in a tissue priming with mutagenic risks.
the BP/DSS model can induce a rapid development of colon adenocarcinomata in mice.
the BP/DSS model provides a useful model for investigating the relationship between the induction of mutations in the colon and subsequent tumor development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BP/DSS model can be used as a rapid and useful colon cancer model.
a high level of mutations in a tissue is not sufficient for tumor induction.
the BP/DSS model is a rapid and useful model of colon carcinogenesis, and that inflammation in a tissue that has been primed with mutagens can lead to tumors in this model.
